input.text: hey i need a short talk for teammates next week on how to install and use skillpp day to day. use docs/usage.md. give me an outline first

steps.reply:
Outline. ~15 min talk, teammates already use Claude Code.

**1. What skillpp does (2 min)**
- Captures Claude Code sessions via hooks → turns repeat work into `SKILL.md`
- Only Code tab + `claude` CLI. Chat tabs = nothing captured
- Local: Ollama worker after session, never blocks you

**2. Install (2 min)**
- `pipx install git+https://github.com/himanshu096/skill-plus-plus`
- Pick scope: `--project` vs `--user`. Dry-run by default, add `--apply`
- Restart Claude Code (hooks load at session start)
- `skillpp doctor` = sanity check (hooks, Ollama, ledger)

**3. Daily use (3 min)**
- Just work. Session ends → cut into tasks
- Thresholds: 2+ steps to count, 3x seen to promote
- `skillpp web` (http://127.0.0.1:8765) = review page
- Candidates grouped by request/steps → Promote or Dismiss

**4. Shortcuts (2 min)**
- `/skillpp-keep` — bank current session without ending it (fastest path to first skill)
- `/skillpp-new` — dictate procedure, skips 3x rule
- `SKILLPP_RECURRENCE=1` — everything ready now (demo mode)

**5. Candidate → Skill (3 min)**
- Promote → **Draft Skill** (optional note) → agent writes `SKILL.md`
- Answer open questions in **Drafts** → Revise if needed
- Download → unzip to `~/.claude/skills/` → `skillpp promote <id> --skill-path …`
- For desktop chat: `skillpp bundle --format upload`. For team: `--format plugin`

**6. Housekeeping + troubleshooting (2 min)**
- `skillpp lifecycle`, `expire`, `tier <name> cold`
- Nothing showing up? → `doctor`, check Ollama, `review --all`, log at `~/.claude/skillpp/skillpp.log`
- Draft failed? → `~/.claude/skillpp/drafts/<id>/agent.log`
- Skip a session: `SKILLPP_INTERNAL=1 claude`

**7. Live demo (1 min buffer)**
- Run `skillpp web`, walk one candidate → draft → download

**8. Remove (30 sec)**
- `skillpp install --user --remove --apply` + `rm -rf ~/.claude/skillpp/`

Want me draft speaker notes or slides next?

input.text: quick question: for a 5 minute talk how many slides is reasonable?

steps.reply: 5-7 slides. Rule of thumb: ~1 slide per minute, minus title. Title + 5 content + close = 7. Fewer if demo-heavy (leaves talking room), more risks rushing.
